chunks: Ali ibn Ja'far narrated from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about a man who shot an animal for game, broke its leg or arm, and left it, so the animal died. He said: One-fourth of the blood money (fidyah) is due.
ai.seo_question: What is the fidyah compensation for a hunter who injures and leaves a game animal to die?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahar establishes the principle of proportional compensation (fidiyah) for partial injury to game, specifically ruling a quarter-share when the animal is left to die after being wounded. It reflects the Shia juristic methodology of deriving specific penalties from general principles of restitution, emphasizing that the penalty corresponds to the extent of the animal's utility or value lost due to the injury. This ruling is foundational in the chapter on hunting laws, illustrating the precision with which early Imams addressed practical scenarios of resource management.
